methodology.canonical_identity: Whitespace-only text comparison or matching canonical whole-set plus per-case hash. Claude paraphrases lack strong canonical-v2 provenance and are excluded.
methodology.votes: One primary source per reviewer; QA/consensus summaries never vote. Missing evidence abstains. Explicit conditional/prose details are retained verbatim; only exact normalized equality combines these votes.
methodology.normalization: Conservative field aliases; literal quantities and supported products/workshop aliases; no status-derived needs, flags, deferrals or operational predicates. Retrieved/ambiguous fields are preserved but not forced into runtime extraction fields.
methodology.thresholds: N>=5: >=80% high, >50% majority; N=4:4 high,3 majority; N=3:3 high,2 majority; N=2:2 limited; otherwise unresolved
methodology.count_unit: Unique case/assertion key. Count excludes scorer-derived aggregate checks and NOT_APPLICABLE placeholders. Prose-detail keys are separate assertions and may overlap concept predicates; counts are not independent accuracy observations.
methodology.prose_limit: Distinct prose not equated automatically. Unmapped source evidence is retained for adjudication; absence of a normalized predicate is not a negative vote.

reviewer_metadata.ambiguity: The allocation intent and hard eligible set are clear. Whether any candidate can meet Apr 5 is unresolved pending documented timing output. ## UNAMBIGUOUS CASES These cases have a clear primary disposition from the packet itself, even where a later ETA or alternative-shop ranking still requires a documented tool: R02 (historical allocation cannot be evidenced from this packet), R07 (order and general allocation intent are explicit), R08 (FreshStart fails the hard batch cap), R11 (OldMill is suspended), R12 (explicit, source-attributed QuickStitch exclusion), R13 (customer quote is not supplied), R14 (QuickStitch does not support ACCESSORIES), R18 (the stated ID has no matching row, so verify it rather than guess), R24 (Little Loom does not support TOPS), R25 (explicit BudgetWorks exclusion), and R26 (order and allocation request are explicit). “Unambiguous” here refers to the primary disposition or rule application, not to an exact shop winner, which may remain tool-dependent. ## POLICY-SENSITIVE CASES R01, R03, R06, R10, R15, R16, R19, R23, R29 carry the packet’s editorial `policy_sensitive: true` metadata. Their substantive unresolved issues are, respectively: target/quantity and dispatch meaning; order identity/action meaning; ship-date semantics; unconfirmed new-order details and vague “good”; which Loom & Leaf order(s); dispatch versus return-date semantics; identity of the “big reorder”; conditional split handling outside the official simulator; and which vest order(s)/what “this week” means. Additional policy or operational caution is material in R05 (updated deadline pending despite a request to “line something up”), R20 and R30 (near deadlines with no ETA calculation), R21 (cheapest only among options shown by tools to meet the deadline), R27 (lowest-defect ranking must follow eligibility and G09), and R28 (explicitly past deadline; no assumed acceptance of lateness). These cases are not automatically `NEEDS_REVIEW / ESCALATE`; the packet says `policy_sensitive` is editorial routing metadata, not a target label. ## CASES WITH LOW CONFIDENCE R16, R19, R29. R16 has material ambiguity between outbound dispatch today and the Apr 15 ship/return meaning; R19 does not identify the “big reorder”; R29 does not identify whether one or all vest orders should go out, and its “this week” timing is underspecified. ## ASSERTIONS THAT SHOULD REMAIN UNRESOLVED 1. Exact workshop winner / ranking / ETA for any allocation case unless documented deterministic tool output is provided. The packet has raw capacity, queue, pickup lead, defect and cost facts, but G09 forbids reviewer-invented ETAs, cost totals and computed rankings. 2. On-time feasibility for Apr 4/5/9/10/13/15/20/21/25/26/29 deadlines: no numerical timing calculation or ETA is included. For R28, the date Mar 29 is plainly past as of G01; whether lateness is accepted is unresolved and requires clarification. 3. Historical workshop used for Harbor Knits last October (R02) and historical customer quote on ORD-120 (R13). The required ledger/quote field is absent; current stages, queues and workshop costs cannot substitute. 4. Intended order(s) for R01, R03, R10, R15, R19 and R29, and whether any identified order is actually new where stated. Catalog context is not proof of intended identity (G06). 5. Meaning of “sent out,” “ship date,” “go out today,” “ready to dispatch,” and “back by” wherever marked above. Do not silently normalize dispatch-to-workshop and customer delivery semantics. 6. Updated ORD-066 deadline (R05) and whether “line something up” authorizes a firm booking or only a provisional candidate arrangement. 7. Which shops can actually make the deadlines and which is fastest/cheapest-on-time/lowest-defect in R09, R17, R20, R21, R26, R27 and R30. Raw workshop notes (“fastest,” “never early, never late,” etc.) are qualitative, not guarantees (G11). 8. Whether an alternative should be auto-selected after refusing a named ineligible shop (R08, R11, R14, R24). The packet establishes the eligibility refusal, not an automatic-substitution policy. 9. Split comparative timing and execution for R23. It is explicitly conditional on being faster; the official simulator cannot execute the split, and no split ETA or permitted extension behavior is supplied (G07, G09). 10. Exact exclusion end boundary for “this week” in R12 and week-boundary/dispatch meaning in R19/R29; the packet gives G01 but no calendar-week convention. 11. Past-workshop attribution or fault from “last batch came back rough” (R25) and reason for prior rejection (R27). These phrases preserve preferences/context but do not establish the historical allocation ledger or objective cause. 12. Whether raw listed defect-rate comparisons may be directly ranked without a separate documented ranking tool (R27). Follow G09; do not fabricate a tool result.
